elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Renewal remains automatic ("Each Service Option Attachment will renew automatically"), and the conditional automatic-renewal elements are not all satisfied: the renewal term still equals the prior term (not fixed at 12 months), opt-out is 60 rather than 30 days, there is no Vendor reminder, and the uplift cap is 105% rather than the lesser of CPI and 3%. No mutual-written-agreement renewal alternative was inserted.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Retained language renews "for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term"; if any Service Option Attachment or Order Form term exceeds twelve months the renewal term will too. To meet this, replace the duration formula with "for successive terms of twelve (12) months".

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered clause requires notice "at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term" — 60 days exceeds the 30-day preferred ceiling.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation appears anywhere in the rendered Section 3.2 or 13.1 text; a sentence requiring IBM to notify Customer at least 60 days before each renewal date would be needed.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Inserted cap is "will not exceed 105% of the charges in effect for the immediately preceding term" — a flat 5% ceiling, not the lesser of CPI and 3%.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Operation 1 changed "ninety (90) days" to "sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term"; the window is exactly 60 days, at the fallback ceiling. The deterministic check reporting "number not found" is a parsing artefact — the spelled-out figure "sixty (60)" is present in the operative text.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "Charges for each renewal term will not exceed 105% of the charges in effect for the immediately preceding term of the applicable Service Option Attachment" — a 5% ceiling on each renewal uplift. Section 13.1's separate mid-term price-change right (with Customer's no-charge termination election) is a different mechanic and does not remove the renewal cap.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the non-renewal window is reduced to exactly 60 days and renewal uplift is capped at 105% of the prior term's charges.

Preferred level fails on four counts — no 12-month renewal-term limit, 60-day rather than 30-day opt-out, no 60-day Vendor renewal reminder, and a 5% cap instead of the lesser of CPI and 3%. These are correctly noted in the rationale rather than redlined.

Minimality holds: only the notice figure was altered and one concise cap sentence added; Section 13.1's change right, non-retroactivity and Customer's 30-day no-charge termination election are retained verbatim, and no survival tails, procedures or extra requirements were bolted on.

Intent is preserved: no defined term, cross-reference or commercial mechanic is left dangling, and the retained 13.1 price-change right is reconcilable with the renewal-specific cap (13.1 governs in-term changes; the new sentence governs the renewal uplift).

Residual risk worth noting to the drafter (not a checklist defect): because renewal terms still mirror the prior term's duration, a multi-year initial term would produce automatic multi-year renewals, which sits in walk-away territory under this rule. If any Order Form term exceeds twelve months, escalate and fix renewals at twelve months.

Optional hardening if IBM pushes back: consider clarifying that a Section 13.1 price change taking effect at a renewal date is subject to the 105% renewal cap, to foreclose an argument that 13.1 supplies an uncapped route to the same increase.
